dedupe_keys.name: cancpld convective parameters and lightning data to support future thunderstorm projections in north america

description: CanCPLD: Convective Parameters and Lightning Data to Support Future Thunderstorm Projections in North America is a data set described in a peer-reviewed Scientific Data article written by Alex J. Cannon et al. Thunderstorms cause natural hazards, including hail, floods, strong winds, and lightning. Simulating thunderstorms in climate models is challenging due to their small scale, the complexity of their physical drivers, and the need to parameterize subgrid processes. Thunderstorm activity can be inferred by identifying relevant historical environmental parameters, e.g. Coverage: continental; published in 2025. Formats: NetCDF. The only repository address found in the article is the code repository in Zenodo named in its Code Availability section; the data may be hosted elsewhere, as the Data Records section of the article states. Access is free of charge and open according to the article. The licence is CC-BY-4.0, taken from DataCite rights of the deposit. Caveats: written from the Scientific Data article metadata (title, abstract, Data Records section) read on 2026-10-01; the data themselves were not opened or downloaded, so their contents, quality and current availability were not checked. It can support industrial-facility and resource studies. Related records: none catalogued yet.
